paras: The hanging of three Mexican men on the Bandera road was the killing of three unnamed men whose bodies were found hanging from a tree northwest of San Antonio, Texas, on or shortly before 17 December 1881. The men were supposed to be robbers of travelers, and the papers said they had probably been lynched by German farmers of the neighborhood. Distant papers reported it only through a brief telegraphic item, and no one was identified.

A report received at San Antonio on Saturday evening, 17 December, said that the bodies of three Mexicans had been found hanging to a tree on the "Bandero road, northwest of there." According to that report, they were supposed to be the three men who had been robbing travelers in the section during the past week. Who hanged them was not established; the dispatch said only that they were "thought to have been hanged by German farmers." The coverage gives no names for the dead, no time for the hanging, and no account of how the men were taken.
No report of an inquest, an arrest or any official response appears in the coverage.

The story ran on 19 and 20 December as one or two sentences in telegraphic columns, among accidents, fires and crimes from across the country. The Sacramento Daily Record-Union printed the fullest version and also reduced it to a single line in its morning news summary, placing the tree "near San Antonio." The Silver State of Unionville, Nevada, reprinted the same dispatch nearly word for word.

The Dallas Daily Herald, the only Texas paper found to carry it, placed the bodies "near Bandera, this State" and went further than the wire text, stating that the men "were probably lynched by the citizens, German farmers, of the neighborhood." No paper questioned the robbery suspicion or commented on the killing, and none named the victims beyond calling them "Mexicans."

reader.title: Hanging of three Mexican men on the Bandera road
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: Three men were found hanged from a tree and a Texas paper said they were 'probably lynched' by local farmers as supposed robbers (A4, A5).

Three men were hanged with no lawful process reported, and the papers supposed they were robbers punished by 'German farmers' or 'the citizens' (A4, A5); the hangers were never identified or counted, so the group and its size rest on supposition.
All versions trace to one report received at San Antonio and carried by telegraph (A3, A4, A5, A6); no local, inquest or follow-up account was found.
